definitions.explanation: The audible sound of someone laughing. Focuses on the sound itself rather than the act of laughing.

examples.japanese: {笑|わら}い{声|ごえ}が{聞|き}こえる。
{子|こ}どもたちの{笑|わら}い{声|ごえ}が{公園|こうえん}に{響|ひび}いた。
examples.english: Children's laughter echoed through the park.

examples.japanese: {隣|となり}の{部屋|へや}から{大|おお}きな{笑|わら}い{声|ごえ}が{漏|も}れてきて、{気|き}になって{眠|ねむ}れなかった。
examples.english: Loud laughter was coming from the next room, and it bothered me so much I couldn't sleep.

notes:
A compound of {笑|わら}い (laughing) and {声|こえ} (voice/sound), where {声|こえ} becomes {声|ごえ} through rendaku. This word emphasizes the audible aspect of laughter — what you hear — rather than the facial expression or the act of laughing itself.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {笑|わら}い{声|ごえ}が{聞|き}こえる: to hear laughter
- {笑|わら}い{声|ごえ}が{響|ひび}く: laughter echoes/rings out
- {笑|わら}い{声|ごえ}を{上|あ}げる: to raise a laugh, to burst out laughing
- {大|おお}きな{笑|わら}い{声|ごえ}: loud laughter
- {笑|わら}い{声|ごえ}が{止|と}まらない: can't stop laughing

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {笑|わら}い: laughter, a laugh — the act or fact of laughing, broader than the sound
- {哄笑|こうしょう}: roar of laughter — literary, describing loud group laughter
- {微笑|びしょう}: smile — visual rather than audible

RELATED PATTERNS:
The ～{声|ごえ} pattern creates many sound-related nouns: {泣|な}き{声|ごえ} (crying sound), {叫|さけ}び{声|ごえ} (shout), {話|はな}し{声|ごえ} (speaking voice).
